shortlist.label: Odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the description of a hard, mineralized structure and is a common cause of asymptomatic calcified masses on the jaw

shortlist.label: Maxillary exostosis
shortlist.why_kept: Initial diagnostic hypothesis and matches the location and description of the mass

shortlist.label: Osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the discrete radiopaque lesion and is a type of benign bone tumor

shortlist.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the hard, mineralized structure and is a type of benign fibro-osseous lesion

shortlist.label: Complex odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Is a type of odontoma that could explain the complex nature of the mass and its mineralized structure

raw.rationale: The presence of a hard, mineralized structure and a discrete radiopaque lesion on the periapical radiograph, along with the location on the right anterior maxilla, supports the diagnosis of maxillary exostosis, which is a benign bony growth.

rejected.label: Odontoma
rejected.why: Odontoma is typically associated with unerupted teeth and is not usually described as a single, discrete mineralized structure.

rejected.label: Osteoma
rejected.why: Osteoma is a benign bone tumor, but it is less common in the maxilla and does not typically present with mucosal fenestration.

rejected.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: Cemento-ossifying fibroma is a more aggressive lesion that often presents with symptoms and rapid growth, which is not consistent with the asymptomatic and stable nature of this case.

rejected.label: Complex odontoma
rejected.why: Complex odontoma is a type of odontoma that typically presents as a collection of small, disorganized tooth structures, which does not match the description of a single, hard, mineralized structure in this case.
